extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants, securities lawyers, auditors, accountants, and compliance officers preparing SEC filings
extracted.subtask_description: Regulation S-K Subpart 229.1500 disclosure requirements and related Article 14 financial-disclosure rules for climate-related risks, GHG metrics, targets, governance, risk management, and attestation to be included in SEC filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of calculation for Article 14 financial effects
rubrics_metrics.description: When calculating the financial statement effects in this Article 14, except where otherwise indicated, a registrant must: (1) Use financial information that is consistent with the scope of its consolidated financial statements included in the filing; and (2) Apply the same accounting principles that it is required to apply in the preparation of its consolidated financial statements included in the filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the required basis for computing any financial statement effects disclosed under Article 14; use the same consolidation scope and accounting principles as in the filing's consolidated financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods to be disclosed (Article 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure must be provided for the registrant's most recently completed fiscal year, and to the extent previously disclosed or required to be disclosed, for the historical fiscal year(s), for which audited consolidated financial statements are included in the filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the most recent fiscal year and prior historical fiscal year(s) as applicable when those years are covered by audited consolidated financial statements in the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual information for severe weather effects (§210.14-02(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide contextual information, describing how each specified financial statement effect disclosed under §210.14-02(b) through (h) was derived, including a description of significant inputs and assumptions used, significant judgments made, other information that is important to understand the financial statement effect and, if applicable, policy decisions made by the registrant to calculate the specified disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe derivation, inputs, assumptions, judgments, important contextual facts and policy choices used to calculate disclosed financial effects from severe weather/other natural conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure thresholds for expenditures expensed and losses (§210.14-02(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of the aggregate amount of expenditures expensed as incurred and losses pursuant to paragraph (c) of this section is required if the aggregate amount of expenditures expensed as incurred and losses equals or exceeds one percent of the absolute value of income or loss before income tax expense or benefit for the relevant fiscal year. Such disclosure is not required, however, if the aggregate amount of expenditures expensed as incurred and losses is less than $100,000 for the relevant fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute aggregate expenditures/losses and compare to 1% of absolute pre-tax income (or $100,000 minimum threshold) to determine if disclosure is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure thresholds for capitalized costs and charges (§210.14-02(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of the aggregate amount of capitalized costs and charges pursuant to paragraph (d) of this section is required if the aggregate amount of the absolute value of capitalized costs and charges equals or exceeds one percent of the absolute value of stockholders' equity or deficit at the end of the relevant fiscal year. Such disclosure is not required, however, if the aggregate amount of the absolute value of capitalized costs and charges is less than $500,000 for the relevant fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare aggregate capitalized costs/charges to 1% of absolute stockholders' equity (or $500,000 minimum) to decide on required disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expenditures expensed and losses from severe weather (Article 14 §210.14-02(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the aggregate amount of expenditures expensed as incurred and losses, excluding recoveries, incurred during the fiscal year as a result of severe weather events and other natural conditions (examples: restore operations, relocate assets, retire/repair/impair affected assets, or otherwise respond). Disclosure must separately identify where the expenditures expensed as incurred and losses are presented in the income statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide aggregate figure(s), exclude recoveries, give examples of included items, and separately identify income-statement presentation location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalized costs and charges from severe weather (Article 14 §210.14-02(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the aggregate amount of capitalized costs and charges, excluding recoveries, incurred during the fiscal year as a result of severe weather events and other natural conditions (examples: restore operations, retire/replace/repair assets, recognize impairment). Disclosure must separately identify where the capitalized costs and charges are presented in the balance sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide aggregate capitalized costs/charges excluding recoveries and identify balance-sheet presentation location; include relevant examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carbon offsets and RECs financial disclosure (Article 14 §210.14-02(e)(1)-(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If carbon offsets or RECs have been used as a material component of a registrant's plans to achieve its disclosed climate-related targets or goals, disclose the aggregate amount of carbon offsets and RECs expensed, the aggregate amount of capitalized carbon offsets and RECs recognized, and the aggregate amount of losses incurred on the capitalized carbon offsets and RECs, during the fiscal year. Also disclose the beginning and ending balances of the capitalized carbon offsets and RECs for the fiscal year; and state the registrant's accounting policy for carbon offsets and RECs as part of contextual information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose amounts expensed, capitalized, losses, opening/closing balances, presentation locations in income statement/balance sheet, and the accounting policy for offsets/RECs whenever they are a material component of plans to meet targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recoveries disclosure (Article 14 §210.14-02(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant is required to provide disclosure pursuant to paragraphs (c) or (d), then as part of contextual information the registrant must state separately the aggregate amount of any recoveries recognized during the fiscal year as a result of severe weather events and other natural conditions for which capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, or losses are disclosed. Disclosure must separately identify where the recoveries are presented in the income statement and the balance sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report aggregate recoveries separately and identify their financial-statement presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution rule for including amounts (Article 14 §210.14-02(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of providing disclosure pursuant to paragraphs (c), (d), and (f), a capitalized cost, expenditure expensed, charge, loss, or recovery results from a severe weather event or other natural condition when the event or condition is a significant contributing factor in incurring the item. If an event or condition is a significant contributing factor in incurring a cost, expenditure, charge, loss, or recovery, then the entire amount of such item must be included in the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the event is a 'significant contributing factor' include the full amount in disclosures (no pro rata allocation required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of financial estimates and assumptions materially impacted (Article 14 §210.14-02(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose whether the estimates and assumptions the registrant used to produce the consolidated financial statements were materially impacted by exposures to risks and uncertainties associated with, or known impacts from, severe weather events and other natural conditions, or any climate-related targets or transition plans disclosed by the registrant. If yes, provide a qualitative description of how the development of such estimates and assumptions were impacted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether estimates/assumptions were materially impacted by severe weather/climate targets/transition plans and qualitatively describe the impacts on development of those estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit requirement: Letter re GHG emissions attestation provider (Item 601 Exhibit Table)
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 601 Exhibit Table includes entry (27) 'Letter re GHG emissions attestation provider' as an exhibit required for many registration and Exchange Act forms (e.g., S-1, S-3, S-4, F-1, 10-K, 10-Q, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicable, registrants must include Exhibit (27) about a GHG emissions attestation provider with registration statements or reports as specified in the exhibit table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter re GHG emissions attestation report (Item 601(b)(27))
rubrics_metrics.description: A letter, where applicable, from the attestation provider that acknowledges awareness of the use in a registration statement of a GHG emissions attestation report that pursuant to 17 CFR 230.436(i)(1) (Rule 436(i)(1)) under the Securities Act is not considered a part of a registration statement prepared or certified by a person within the meaning of sections 7 and 11 of the Securities Act. Such letter may be filed with the registration statement, an amendment thereto, or a report on Form 10-K, Form 10-Q, or Form 20-F, which is incorporated by reference into the registration statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required letter must acknowledge the Rule 436(i)(1) status and may be filed with the registration statement or specified periodic reports incorporated by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions used in Subpart 229.1500
rubrics_metrics.description: The subpart defines terms including: Carbon offsets; Climate-related risks (physical, acute, chronic, transition risks); Carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e); Emission factor; GHG or Greenhouse gases; GHG emissions (direct and indirect); Internal carbon price; Operational boundaries; Organizational boundaries; Renewable energy credit/certificate (REC); Scenario analysis; Scope 1 emissions; Scope 2 emissions; Transition plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions to interpret disclosure requirements (e.g., operational/organizational boundaries affect GHG calculations; scope definitions determine which emissions to disclose). The regulation provides detailed definitions and examples for each term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance disclosure (Item 1501)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the board of directors' oversight of climate-related risks, identify any board committee or subcommittee responsible, and describe the processes by which the board or such committee is informed. If there is a climate-related target/goal or transition plan, describe whether and how the board oversees progress. Describe management's role in assessing and managing material climate-related risks, addressing: (1) which management positions/committees are responsible and their relevant expertise; (2) processes by which they assess/manage risks; and (3) whether they report to the board or committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include detailed description of board oversight, committee responsibilities, information flow, and management roles and relevant expertise (Instruction 2 gives examples of relevant expertise such as prior work experience, degrees, certifications, skills).

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of material climate-related risks (Item 1502(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any climate-related risks that have materially impacted or are reasonably likely to have a material impact on the registrant, including on its strategy, results of operations, or financial condition. Disclose whether such risks are reasonably likely to manifest in the short-term (next 12 months) and separately in the long-term (beyond 12 months). Disclose whether the risk is physical or transition and provide information necessary to understand the nature of the risk and the extent of the registrant's exposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For physical risks specify whether acute or chronic and geographic location and nature of properties/operations; for transition risks specify whether regulatory/technological/market/other and how these factors impact the registrant. Consider jurisdictional GHG commitments where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material impacts on strategy, business model, and outlook (Item 1502(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the actual and potential material impacts of any climate-related risk on the registrant's strategy, business model, and outlook, including impacts on: (1) business operations and locations; (2) products or services; (3) suppliers/purchasers/counterparties to material contracts; (4) activities to mitigate or adapt (e.g., adoption of new technologies); and (5) expenditures for research and development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete descriptions of how identified risks affect business components and potential changes to operations, products, supply chain, mitigation activities, and R&D spending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of climate impacts into strategy, financial planning, capital allocation (Item 1502(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss whether and how the registrant considers the impacts described in response to paragraph (b) as part of its strategy, financial planning, and capital allocation, including whether impacts have been integrated into the business model and how resources are being used to mitigate climate-related risks and how targets/transition plans relate to the business model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain concrete integration steps (e.g., budget reallocations, strategic shifts) and relationships between disclosed targets/transition plans and business strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative and qualitative description of expenditures and financial impacts from strategy activities (Item 1502(d) and 1502(e)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe quantitatively and qualitatively the material expenditures incurred and material impacts on financial estimates and assumptions that directly result from activities to mitigate or adapt to climate-related risks or from a disclosed transition plan. If a transition plan exists, update annual disclosure describing actions taken and how those actions have impacted the registrant's business, results of operations, or financial condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numbers and narrative linking expenditures and changes in financial estimates/assumptions to specific mitigation/adaptation activities or transition-plan actions; update annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenario analysis disclosure (Item 1502(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant uses scenario analysis and, based on results, determines a climate-related risk is reasonably likely to have a material impact, the registrant must describe each such scenario including a brief description of the parameters, assumptions, and analytical choices used, as well as the expected material impacts, including financial impacts, under each scenario.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose scenarios' parameters, assumptions, analytical choices, and expected material and financial impacts for any scenario that drives a materiality determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal carbon price disclosure (Item 1502(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant's use of an internal carbon price is material to how it evaluates and manages a climate-related risk, disclose in units of reporting currency: (i) the price per metric ton of CO2e; and (ii) the total price, including how the total price is estimated to change over the time periods referenced in Item 1502(a). If multiple internal carbon prices are used, provide disclosures for each and reasons for different prices and describe any material differences in scope from organizational boundaries used for GHG calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report price per ton and total monetary impact over time; explain multiple prices and any scope differences from GHG reporting boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk management processes disclosure (Item 1503)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any processes the registrant has for identifying, assessing, and managing material climate-related risks. Address, as applicable: (1) how the registrant identifies whether it has incurred or is reasonably likely to incur a material physical or transition risk; (2) how it decides whether to mitigate, accept, or adapt to the risk; and (3) how it prioritizes whether to address the risk. If managing a material climate-related risk, disclose whether and how these processes have been integrated into the registrant's overall risk management system or processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain identification, decision-making, prioritization, and integration into enterprise-wide risk processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targets and goals disclosure (Item 1504(a)-(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant must disclose any climate-related target or goal if it has materially affected or is reasonably likely to materially affect the registrant's business, results of operations, or financial condition. Provide scope of activities included; unit of measurement; defined time horizon and whether based on treaties/laws/organizations; baseline time period and means of tracking progress; qualitative description of how the registrant intends to meet the target or goal. Disclose progress each fiscal year and actions taken, material impacts resulting from the target or actions, and quantitative and qualitative disclosure of material expenditures and impacts on financial estimates. If carbon offsets or RECs were used as a material component, separately disclose the amount of carbon avoidance/reduction/removal or generated renewable energy, nature and source of offsets/RECs, description and location of underlying projects, registries/authentication, and cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comprehensive disclosures for targets/goals: scope, metrics, timeline, baseline, progress, costs, financial impacts, and, where offsets/RECs are material, detailed project/source/authentication/cost information.

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG emissions metrics required (Item 1505(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that is a large accelerated filer or an accelerated filer must disclose its Scope 1 emissions and/or its Scope 2 emissions, if such emissions are material, for its most recently completed fiscal year and, to the extent previously disclosed in a Commission filing, for the historical fiscal year(s) included in the consolidated financial statements in the filing. Disclose Scope 1 and Scope 2 separately, expressed in aggregate in terms of CO2e, and disclose gross terms (excluding impact of purchased/generated offsets). If any constituent gas is individually material, disclose it disaggregated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large accelerated and accelerated filers must report Scope 1 and/or Scope 2 (if material) in CO2e, separate scopes, gross of offsets, and disaggregate materially individual gases. Smaller reporting companies and emerging growth companies are exempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions and exclusions for GHG metrics (Item 1505(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A smaller reporting company and an emerging growth company are exempt from disclosure requirements of this section. A registrant is not required to include GHG emissions from a manure management system when disclosing Scopes 1 and 2 so long as implementation is subject to restrictions on appropriated funds or otherwise prohibited under federal law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check filer status for exemption; manure-management emissions may be excluded under specified legal restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology, inputs, and assumptions for GHG metrics (Item 1505(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the methodology, significant inputs, and significant assumptions used to calculate the registrant's GHG emissions disclosed: (i) organizational boundaries used and method to determine them (explain material differences from consolidated-financial-statement scope); (ii) operational boundaries including approach to categorization of emissions and emissions sources; and (iii) the protocol or standard used, including calculation approach, type and source of emission factors, and any calculation tools used. Registrants may use reasonable estimates if they describe underlying assumptions and reasons for using estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient detail for a reasonable investor to understand boundaries, categorization, protocols/standards, emission factors, tools, and explain use of estimates and their assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and incorporation of GHG metrics in filings (Item 1505(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: GHG emissions metrics required in an annual report on Form 10-K may be incorporated by reference from the registrant's Form 10-Q for the second fiscal quarter in the fiscal year immediately following the year to which the GHG emissions metrics disclosure relates, or included in an amended annual report on Form 10-K no later than the due date for such Form 10-Q. For registration statements or Form 10/Form 20-F filings, any required GHG emissions metrics must be provided as of the most recently completed fiscal year that is at least 225 days prior to the date of effectiveness of the registration statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specified timing rules for incorporation by reference or amendment; for registration statements ensure metrics date is at least 225 days prior to effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation requirement and phased assurance levels (Item 1506(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant required to provide Scope 1 and/or Scope 2 emissions disclosure must include an attestation report covering such disclosure in the relevant filing, subject to: (i) for accelerated filers beginning the third fiscal year after the compliance date the attestation engagement must be at least limited assurance; (ii) for large accelerated filers beginning the third fiscal year after the compliance date the attestation must be at least limited assurance; and (iii) for large accelerated filers beginning the seventh fiscal year after the compliance date the attestation engagement must be at a reasonable assurance level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attestation is mandatory and assurance levels increase over time per filer category and compliance-year schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation standards requirements (Item 1506(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any attestation report required must be provided pursuant to standards that are: (i) publicly available at no cost or that are widely used for GHG emissions assurance; and (ii) established by a body or group that has followed due process procedures, including broad distribution of the framework for public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use attestation standards that are public/widely used and developed through a due-process body with public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary assurance treatment (Item 1506(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that obtains voluntary assurance over its GHG emissions disclosure prior to the first required fiscal year for assurance must comply with paragraph (e) of this section. Voluntary assurance obtained after the first required fiscal year that is in addition to any required assurance must follow requirements of paragraphs (b) through (d) and must use the same attestation standard as the required assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary assurance before or after the first required year triggers specific compliance obligations and requires using the same standard as required assurance when in addition to required assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications for GHG emissions attestation provider (Item 1506(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A GHG emissions attestation provider must be an expert in GHG emissions by virtue of having significant experience in measuring, analyzing, reporting, or attesting to GHG emissions. Significant experience means having sufficient competence and capabilities to (i) perform engagements in accordance with attestation standards and applicable legal/regulatory requirements; and (ii) enable the service provider to issue reports that are appropriate under the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attestation providers must demonstrate documented experience and competence in GHG engagements sufficient to perform attestation under applicable standards and laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence requirements for attestation provider (Item 1506(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The GHG emissions attestation provider must be independent with respect to the registrant and any of its affiliates during the attestation and professional engagement period. A provider is not independent if it is not, or a reasonable investor would conclude it is not, capable of exercising objective and impartial judgment. The Commission will consider relationships or services that create mutual/conflicting interests, attesting to one's own work, acting as management/employee, or advocacy for the registrant, and all financial or other relationships between provider and registrant/affiliates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate all relationships/services for conflicts, avoid situations where provider acts as advocate or attests to its own work, and consider financial and nonfinancial ties when assessing independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions related to attestation period and affiliates (Item 1506(b)(3)-(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'affiliate' has the meaning provided in §210.2-01, except references to 'audit' are deemed to be references to attestation services. 'Attestation and professional engagement period' means both: (A) the period covered by the attestation report; and (B) the period of the engagement to attest to a registrant's GHG emissions or to prepare a report filed with the Commission. The professional engagement period begins when the attestation service provider signs an initial engagement letter or begins attest procedures, whichever is earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions to determine independence conflicts and the relevant time window for assessing relationships and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation report form and content must follow standard (Item 1506(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The form and content of the attestation report must follow the requirements set forth by the attestation standard (or standards) used by the GHG emissions attestation provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the chosen attestation standard's required report form and content; do not substitute alternative formats that conflict with the standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional disclosure about attestation provider and predecessor engagements (Item 1506(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Large accelerated filers and accelerated filers must disclose, alongside the GHG emissions disclosure, after requesting relevant information from any GHG emissions attestation provider as necessary: (1) whether the provider is subject to any oversight inspection program and if so which program(s) and whether the engagement is included in the scope; and (2)(i) whether any previously engaged provider resigned, declined to stand for re-appointment, or was dismissed (and the date), and (ii) whether there were disagreements with the former provider on any matter of measurement or disclosure of GHG emissions or attestation scope/procedures, including description and whether registrant authorized the former provider to respond to successor inquiries. 'Disagreements' is interpreted broadly to include differences of opinion that would have caused the former provider to reference the subject matter in its report if unresolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose oversight program status of provider and any predecessor-provider resignations/dismissals and disagreements, with broad interpretation of 'disagreements' to include unresolved differences of opinion; describe each disagreement and whether successor was authorized to consult the former provider.
